title: Pricing War Response
description: A competitor launches a free tier matching your core features. You have 2 weeks before the board meeting.

context.company: SaaS startup, $5M ARR, 45% gross margin, 18% annual churn, 50 employees
context.situation: Major competitor (public company, $500M ARR) just launched a free tier that matches 80% of your core features. Your largest customer (15% of revenue) is evaluating switching. Board meeting in 2 weeks.
context.time_pressure: Board meeting in 2 weeks. Need recommendation with financial impact analysis.
data_provided: Current P&L: $5M ARR, 45% GM, $1.2M S&M, $800k R&D, $600k G&A
Customer segments: Enterprise (60% ARR, 5% churn), SMB (40% ARR, 30% churn)
Competitor intel: Free tier has no SSO, no API, 5-user limit, no support
Switching cost analysis: Average 3-month implementation, data export gaps

stages.prompt: What framework(s) should you apply FIRST to diagnose this situation?

options.label: Porter's Five Forces + Competitive Response Matrix
options.rationale: Systematically analyzes competitive position and maps response options against rival's move

options.label: SWOT Analysis only
options.rationale: Too general. Doesn't provide actionable response framework for competitive threat

options.label: Immediate 20% price cut across the board
options.rationale: Reactive, destroys margins, signals weakness, no strategic framework applied

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Provide CEO-grade feedback on framework selection.

stages.prompt: Estimate the quarterly revenue impact if you lose 15% of Enterprise customers and 25% of SMB customers to the free tier. Show your work.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User estimated {response}. Correct: Enterprise $5M×60%×15%=$450k/qtr, SMB $5M×40%×25%=$500k/qtr. Total $950k/qtr ($3.8M ARR at risk). Evaluate their reasoning.
stages.sample_answer: Enterprise $5M×60%×15%=$450k/qtr, SMB $5M×40%×25%=$500k/qtr. Total $950k/qtr ($3.8M ARR at risk).

stages.prompt: Choose your strategic response:

options.label: Differentiate: Launch 'Pro' tier with SSO, API, unlimited users, dedicated support at current price. Keep 'Starter' at $X. Invest in switching cost moats (integrations, data gravity).
options.rationale: Leverages competitor's free tier limitations. Protects Enterprise segment. Builds moats.

options.label: Match: Launch your own free tier. Hope to convert 5% to paid. Accept 30% revenue hit.
options.rationale: Race to bottom. Destroys unit economics. Hard to raise prices later. Signals commoditization.

options.label: Acquire: Buy a complementary tool to bundle. 6-month timeline. $2M cost.
options.rationale: Too slow for immediate threat. Integration risk. Good as secondary play, not primary response.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate strategic logic, financial impact, and execution risk.

stages.prompt: Draft the 2-slide board update: Slide 1 = Situation & Analysis. Slide 2 = Recommendation & Ask.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User drafted {response}. Evaluate clarity, data-driven argument, and board-ready framing.
stages.sample_answer: A good board update includes: 1) Situation summary with key data points, 2) Financial impact analysis with numbers, 3) Proposed response with rationale, 4) Specific ask from the board (approval, guidance, resources). Keep it concise — 2 slides maximum.

optimal.title: Strategic Differentiation Win
optimal.description: Launched Pro tier, retained 95% Enterprise, converted 10% SMB to paid. ARR grew to $6.2M in 6 months. Competitor's free tier became lead gen for you.

acceptable.title: Defensive Hold
acceptable.description: Price-matched selectively, lost 8% revenue short-term but stabilized. Slow bleed risk remains. Need product differentiation within 12 months.

failure.title: Value Destruction
failure.description: Panicked price cuts or free tier launch. Gross margin dropped to 25%. Burn rate unsustainable. Down round or shutdown within 18 months.

title: Acquisition Target Evaluation
description: Evaluate a $15M acquisition target for technology and team. Board needs your recommendation in 1 week.

context.company: Series B SaaS, $12M ARR, $30M cash, 80 employees
context.situation: Target: AI-powered analytics startup, $2M ARR, 15-person team (10 engineers, 3 PhDs), proprietary ML models for predictive analytics. Asking $15M (7.5x ARR). Your product lacks advanced analytics - this would fill a major gap and unlock Enterprise upsell.
context.time_pressure: Exclusivity expires in 1 week. Competitor also looking.
data_provided: Target financials: $2M ARR, 60% GM, $4M burn, 12mo runway, 120% NRR
Your financials: $12M ARR, 70% GM, $2M burn, 15mo runway
Synergy model: $3M ARR upsell in Year 1, $8M by Year 3. Cost synergies: $500k (infra, G&A)
Integration risk: Different tech stack (Python vs your Node), remote team in different timezone, key person risk (2 PhDs)
Comparable transactions: 5-10x ARR for AI/ML tuck-ins

stages.prompt: What financial frameworks are ESSENTIAL for this evaluation?

options.label: DCF + LBO + Synergy Quantification + Earnout Modeling
options.rationale: DCF for standalone value, LBO for leverage capacity, synergy model for strategic value, earnout for risk mitigation

options.label: Revenue multiple comparison only (7.5x vs 5-10x comps)
options.rationale: Ignores cash burn, integration costs, earnout structure, strategic option value

options.label: Gut feel + team assessment
options.rationale: Insufficient for $15M (50% of cash). Board will reject.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain why comprehensive financial modeling is non-negotiable.

stages.prompt: Build the synergy model: Calculate Year 1 combined FCF impact. Assume: Your FCF = $2M. Target FCF = -$2M (burn). Revenue synergies = $3M ARR at 70% GM. Cost synergies = $500k. Integration costs = $1M one-time. Show Year 1 FCF.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User calculated {response}. Correct: $2M + (-$2M) + $2.1M (synergy GP) + $0.5M - $1M = $1.6M combined FCF vs $2M standalone. Dilutive Year 1, accretive Year 2+. Evaluate.
stages.sample_answer: $2M + (-$2M) + $2.1M (synergy GP) + $0.5M - $1M = $1.6M combined FCF vs $2M standalone. Dilutive Year 1, accretive Year 2+.

stages.prompt: Structure the deal. Choose the best structure:

options.label: $10M cash at close + $5M earnout over 2 years tied to ARR milestones ($3M Y1, $8M Y3) + 2-year retention packages for 3 key people
options.rationale: Aligns incentives, mitigates key person risk, pays for performance, preserves cash

options.label: $15M all cash at close. Clean and simple.
options.rationale: 50% of cash gone. No protection if team leaves or tech doesn't integrate. All risk on buyer.

options.label: $5M cash + $10M stock. Shares risk.
options.rationale: Better cash preservation but complex valuation, tax issues, misaligned if stock drops

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate risk allocation, incentive alignment, and cash preservation.

optimal.title: Successful Tuck-in
optimal.description: Earnout achieved. Analytics module launched in 4 months. Enterprise upsell $4M ARR Year 1. Team retained. ROIC > 25% by Year 2.

acceptable.title: Partial Success
acceptable.description: Tech integrated in 8 months (slower). Only 1 PhD stayed. Upsell $2M Year 1. Break-even Year 3. Distraction from core product.

failure.title: Failed Integration
failure.description: Both PhDs left at 12 months. Tech debt unmaintainable. $15M write-down. Enterprise deals lost due to distraction. Cash crisis.

title: Crisis: Major Security Incident
description: Data breach affecting 10,000 customers. 4 hours since discovery. Regulators, customers, board all need communication.

context.company: B2B SaaS, $20M ARR, SOC2 certified, 150 employees
context.situation: Unauthorized access to customer PII database discovered 4 hours ago. ~10,000 records exposed (names, emails, company info - no passwords/financials). Attack vector: compromised contractor credentials. Contained 1 hour ago. Legal says 72-hour notification clock started.
context.time_pressure: 72 hours for regulatory notification. Customers expecting update NOW. Board emergency call in 2 hours.
data_provided: Incident timeline: Detection → Containment → Investigation status
Data scope: 10,000 records, PII categories, no auth/financial data
Root cause (preliminary): Contractor MFA bypass via session hijacking
Regulatory: GDPR (EU customers), CCPA (CA), industry-specific
Customer impact: 3 Enterprise accounts (€2M ARR) in affected set

stages.prompt: First 30 minutes: What are your IMMEDIATE priorities? (Select top 3)

options.label: 1) Confirm containment 2) Activate incident response team 3) Preserve evidence for forensics
options.rationale: Correct priority order: stop bleeding, mobilize, preserve legal position

options.label: 1) Draft customer email 2) Call lawyer 3) Post on Twitter transparency
options.rationale: Communication before containment = misinformation risk. Evidence preservation critical for liability.

options.label: 1) Blame contractor 2) Minimize scope in internal comms 3) Delay notification
options.rationale: Destroys trust, legal exposure, regulatory violations. Career-ending for CEO.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain crisis management priority framework.

stages.prompt: Board call in 30 min. What's your recommendation on customer notification timing?

options.label: Notify affected customers within 24 hours with: what happened, what data, what we're doing, what they should do, dedicated support line
options.rationale: Exceeds regulatory minimum. Builds trust. Controls narrative. Reduces legal liability.

options.label: Wait for full forensic report (5-7 days) then notify
options.rationale: Violates GDPR 72-hour rule. Looks like cover-up. Increases fines 4x. Destroys customer trust.

options.label: Notify only the 3 Enterprise accounts. Keep quiet on others.
options.rationale: Discriminatory notification. Regulatory violation. Leaks inevitable. Reputation destroys company.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain regulatory requirements and trust economics.

optimal.title: Trust Strengthened
optimal.description: Transparent, fast response. Customers appreciate honesty. 0 churn from incident. SOC2 renewed with commendation. Industry case study for crisis done right.

acceptable.title: Managed Crisis
acceptable.description: Met regulatory minimums. Some customer frustration. 2% churn. $200k fines. Reputation recoverable in 12 months.

failure.title: Existential Crisis
failure.description: Delayed/partial notification. GDPR fine €4M. Class action lawsuit. 3 Enterprise accounts churn. Board loses confidence. CEO replaced.

title: Scaling Org from 50 to 200
description: Your startup just raised Series B. You need to double the team in 6 months while maintaining culture and performance.

context.company: Series B SaaS, $8M ARR, 50 employees, remote-first since seed
context.situation: Just closed $20M Series B. Board expects 200 headcount in 18 months. Current: 3-layer org, 5-person leadership team. Culture: high-autonomy, written-first, transparent. Key risk: two key engineers (15-person team managers) showing burnout signs. VP Sales search has failed twice (3 months).
context.time_pressure: Q1 hiring plan due in 2 weeks. All-hands on Friday expecting culture message.
data_provided: Current org chart (3 layers: CEO > 5 leaders > 45 ICs)
Hiring pipeline: 8 open roles, 3 offers out, 2 week average to fill
Engagement survey: 82 eNPS, declining trend
Burnout indicators: 2 managers working weekends, productivity down 15%
Competing offers: 3 engineers received 30%+ salary bumps from FAANG

stages.prompt: What org design framework should guide your scaling plan?

options.label: Span of Control + Layer Analysis: Map optimal spans, add layer where >10 reports. Create new VP roles.
options.rationale: Correct first step. Before hiring, fix structure. Prevents flat-org chaos at 200 people.

options.label: Hire as fast as possible. Structure will sort itself out.
options.rationale: Recipe for chaos. No reporting clarity = decision paralysis and culture breakdown.

options.label: Implement matrix org with dotted lines to all VPs
options.rationale: Over-engineered for 200 people. Matrix orgs need strong PM culture and 500+ headcount to justify overhead.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain org design principles for scaling stages.

stages.prompt: VP Sales hiring has failed twice. Both candidates looked great on paper but quit within 60 days. Options:

options.label: Promote internal: top-performing rep with 3 yrs tenure, 180% quota. Give them 6-month trial as interim VP with outsourced coach. Hire strong #2.
options.rationale: Internal knows product/customers. Trial period derisks. Coach fills gaps. Better than empty seat for 9 months.

options.label: Hire external search firm, raise comp to 90th percentile, accept 3-month search timeline
options.rationale: Two failures suggest selection problem, not comp. 3 months empty = missed pipeline.

options.label: Merge Sales under VP Marketing. One fewer hire.
options.rationale: Different skill sets. Marketing lacks enterprise sales experience. Overloads existing leader.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate talent strategy trade-offs: speed vs. fit, internal vs. external, cost of vacancy.

stages.prompt: Two team managers showing burnout (weekend work, productivity drop). Team of 30 engineers depend on them. What do you do?

options.label: 1) Immediate: 2-week mandated PTO 2) Structural: Split each 15-person team into two 7-person teams with new managers promoted from within 3) Culture: Publicly model 'no weekend work' norm
options.rationale: Addresses root cause (oversized teams) while providing immediate relief. Models desired behavior.

options.label: Give them each a 20% raise and equity refresh. They deserve it for working hard.
options.rationale: Rewards harmful behavior. Burnout won't be solved by money. Reinforces 'martyr hero' culture.

options.label: Replace them. If they can't handle startup pace, find people who can.
options.rationale: Career-ending mistake. Top performers burning out = structural problem, not motivation problem. Replacing loses institutional knowledge.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain burnout prevention and team scaling principles.

optimal.title: Scaled Strong
optimal.description: 200 people in 18 months. Culture preserved. eNPS climbed to 85. Attrition under 8%. IPO-ready org.

acceptable.title: Growing Pains
acceptable.description: 165 people in 18 months (missed target). Some culture erosion in middle layers. Attrition 15%. Correctable.

failure.title: Culture Collapse
failure.description: Both managers left. VP Sales still empty. 35% attrition. eNPS dropped to 35. Series B runway wasted on recruiting churn.

title: Platform vs Feature Investment
description: Your CTO wants 6 months for a platform rewrite. Your VP Product wants to ship 3 new features that paying customers are asking for. You have 40 engineers.

context.company: B2B SaaS, $15M ARR, 40 engineers, monolithic Rails app
context.situation: CTO: 'Tech debt is slowing us down. Deploy frequency dropped from daily to weekly. 30% of sprint capacity on bug fixes. We need 6 months to extract core services.' VP Product: '3 enterprise logos ($5M ARR) require SSO, audit logs, and custom reporting to close. Miss these and we miss Q4 targets.'
context.time_pressure: Q4 planning meeting in 3 days. Engineering morale dropping. Customer escalations up.
data_provided: DORA metrics: Deploy freq 1/week (down from daily), Lead time 5 days, CFR 18% (up from 8%), MTTR 4 hours
Engineering morale: 45 eNPS (down from 72), 3 regrettable losses this quarter
Customer pipeline: 3 deals worth $5M ARR blocked by missing features
Platform scope: 6 months, $2M eng cost, projected 3x velocity after
Feature scope: 2 months each, $600k eng cost, unlocks $5M ARR

stages.prompt: Apply the Tech Debt Quadrant. What kind of debt is this?

options.label: Prudent-Deliberate: Original decisions were reasonable at the time. Now constraints changed and the architecture no longer fits.
options.rationale: Rails monolith was correct for first 5 years. At $15M ARR with enterprise customers, the architecture needs to evolve.

options.label: Reckless-Deliberate: CTO knowingly cut corners to ship faster.
options.rationale: No evidence of corner-cutting. Monolith was the right architecture at $1-5M ARR. Context changed.

options.label: Not tech debt - it's feature requests. Ship the features.
options.rationale: DORA metrics deterioration is real tech debt. 18% CFR means 1 in 5 deployments breaks something. Unsustainable.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain the tech debt quadrant and appropriate response per quadrant.

stages.prompt: With 40 engineers, how do you allocate?

options.label: 70/30 split: 28 engineers on features (SSO, audit, custom reporting) targeting 2-month delivery. 12 engineers on platform (extract 2 core services). Review at 2 months.
options.rationale: Addresses both needs simultaneously. Features unblock revenue. Platform investment starts. 2-month review gates commitment.

options.label: 100% platform: Full rewrite for 6 months. No new features.
options.rationale: Loses $5M ARR deals. Customers leave. 6 months without customer value = morale collapse and churn.

options.label: 100% features: Ship all 3 features in 6 months (~13 engineers each). Ignore platform.
options.rationale: Tech debt compounds. 18% CFR will become 30%. Good engineers leave. Features eventually grind to halt.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain the dual-track approach: how to balance innovation and maintenance investment.

stages.prompt: Engineering morale (eNPS 45, 3 losses). What do you do about the team?

options.label: 1) Share the dual-track plan transparently 2) Give each track a strong TL with decision rights 3) Protect 'no-interrupt' deep work blocks 4) Commit to quarterly retro on approach
options.rationale: Transparent plan + autonomy + protected time + feedback loop. Addresses root causes: uncertainty, lack of agency, context switching.

options.label: Announce 'crunch mode' for next 3 months. Free dinner and Uber credits.
options.rationale: Perks don't fix burnout. Crunch mode accelerates attrition. Engineers with options will leave.

options.label: Hire 10 more engineers. More capacity = less pressure.
options.rationale: Brooks' Law: adding people to late projects makes them later. Onboarding load on current team. Doesn't fix root cause.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate engineering team health interventions.

optimal.title: Dual Track Success
optimal.description: 2 features shipped in 3 months ($5M ARR closed). 2 services extracted in 5 months. DORA back to elite. Morale recovered to 70 eNPS.

acceptable.title: Tense Balance
acceptable.description: 1 feature delayed. Platform 1 month behind. Morale stable at 55. Tension between product and platform ongoing. Revenue $3M.

failure.title: Engineer Exodus
failure.description: Crunch mode burned out 12 engineers. Platform stalled. Features buggy (CFR 25%). 3 enterprise deals lost. Rebuild from smaller team.

title: Root Cause: Customer Churn Spike
description: Monthly churn doubled from 3% to 6% in 30 days. No product changes, no pricing changes, no competitor launches. Find the root cause.

context.situation: Churn spiked from 3% to 6% last month. No obvious trigger: no product changes, no pricing changes, no competitor launch. Support tickets up 40%. NPS dropped from 45 to 28. Sales team reports longer close cycles. Engineering says 'no major outages.'
context.time_pressure: Board update in 5 days. If churn stays at 6%, $600k ARR at risk this quarter.
data_provided: Churn by segment: Enterprise (2% > 4%), Mid-market (3% > 5%), SMB (6% > 15%)
Support tickets: 'onboarding' issues up 80%, 'data import' up 50%
Onboarding time: 45 days (was 30 days) per new customer
Customer success team: same 4 people, caseload up from 50 to 75 accounts each
NPS verbatims: 'too hard to set up', 'took 2 months to go live', 'training was insufficient'

stages.prompt: Which cause analysis method should you apply FIRST to identify the root cause?

options.label: Fishbone Diagram + 5 Whys: Categorize causes (People, Process, Technology, Measurement), then drill into each with 5 Whys
options.rationale: Multi-factor problem (both segments and support data suggest multiple contributors). Fishbone organizes, 5 Whys drills.

options.label: Fire the Head of Customer Success. Churn is their job.
options.rationale: Blaming before understanding = toxic culture + wrong fix. Data suggests systemic issue, not individual.

options.label: Run an A/B test on different onboarding flows
options.rationale: Too slow for 6% monthly churn. Need diagnosis before treatment. A/B test takes 2-3 months.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain which cause analysis method fits this problem type.

stages.prompt: Apply the Fishbone. Categorize the data into People, Process, Technology, and Measurement buckets. What pattern emerges?
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User analyzed {response}. Pattern: Process (onboarding stretched from 30 to 45 days because caseload doubled) and Measurement (no leading indicator for churn - only caught at cancellation). Root cause: Customer Success team didn't scale with customer growth. Caseload 50 > 75 = 50% increase in accounts per CSM. Onboarding time degradation directly correlates with churn spike.
stages.sample_answer: Process (onboarding stretched from 30 to 45 days because caseload doubled) and Measurement (no leading indicator for churn - only caught at cancellation).

stages.prompt: Given root cause is CS team overloaded (not scaled with growth). Choose your action:

options.label: 1) Immediate: Hire 2 CSMs, reduce caseload to 50 2) Process: Implement onboarding automation (self-service portal, email sequences) for first 14 days 3) Measurement: Add 'time-to-first-value' and 'onboarding completion' as leading churn indicators
options.rationale: Addresses all three levels: capacity (hire), efficiency (automate), monitoring (metrics). Systemic fix.

options.label: Just hire 4 more CSMs. More people = problem solved.
options.rationale: Capacity fix but no process improvement. Same problem at next growth stage. Hiring lag = continued churn.

options.label: Offer 20% discount to at-risk customers. Buy time.
options.rationale: Treats symptom (churn) not cause (poor onboarding). Revenue loss + same problem persists. Customers leave anyway.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate systemic vs symptomatic solutions to root cause.

optimal.title: Root Cause Fixed
optimal.description: Caseload reduced to 50. Onboarding automated for first 14 days. Time-to-value dropped to 25 days. Churn back to 3% in 3 months. Leading indicators now caught early.

acceptable.title: Symptom Managed
acceptable.description: Hired 2 CSMs but onboarding still manual. Churn dropped to 4% (not 3%). Process debt accumulating. Same problem at 800 customers.

failure.title: Spiral Continues
failure.description: Discounted churning customers. They left anyway after discount period. CS team burned out (2 quit). Churn hit 8%. ARR declining.

title: Runway & Unit Economics Crisis
description: Burn is $400k/mo with 8 months runway. CAC spiked and payback blew past 18 months. Board wants a 90-day plan.

context.company: B2B SaaS, $4.8M ARR, 55 employees, Series A, $3.2M cash
context.situation: Monthly burn hit $400k (was $280k six months ago). Net new ARR slowed from $250k to $80k/mo. CAC rose from $8k to $14k; LTV/CAC fell from 4.2x to 2.1x. Payback now 19 months. Two enterprise deals slipped. Board meeting in 10 days demands a cash and growth plan.
context.time_pressure: 8 months runway at current burn. Board wants 90-day plan with kill/keep decisions.
data_provided: P&L: ARR $4.8M, GM 68%, S&M $2.1M annualized, R&D $1.4M, G&A $0.9M
Unit economics: CAC $14k, avg ACV $22k, gross retention 88%, NRR 102%
Funnel: SQL +12% QoQ but win rate -8pts; sales cycle 72 days (was 55)
Cohorts: last 2 cohorts LTV -25% vs prior year; expansion lagging
Headcount: 12 AE/SDR, 8 CS, 18 eng, 17 other; open reqs: 4 eng, 2 AE

stages.prompt: What should you diagnose FIRST before cutting or fundraising?

options.label: Unit economics by segment + contribution margin by channel + 13-week cash forecast
options.rationale: Separates structural unit-econ problems from temporary funnel noise and quantifies cash options.

options.label: Immediately cut 20% headcount across all departments
options.rationale: Blind cuts destroy growth capacity and morale without fixing CAC or payback root causes.

options.label: Raise a bridge round at any valuation to buy 18 months
options.rationale: May be necessary later, but without a plan and cleaned unit economics you dilute into a worse story.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate whether diagnosis precedes capital structure decisions.

stages.prompt: Estimate months of runway if you cut burn by $120k/mo starting next month (one-time severance $180k). Show remaining cash path.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User estimated {response}. Correct path: start cash $3.2M; month 1 burn $400k + severance $180k = out $580k → $2.62M; then burn $280k/mo → $2.62M / $280k ≈ 9.4 months additional after month 1 (≈10 months total from now vs 8). Evaluate arithmetic and framing.
stages.sample_answer: Start $3.2M. Month 1: burn $400k + severance $180k → cash $2.62M. Ongoing burn $280k → ~9.4 months after month 1 (~10 months total runway vs 8 at status quo).

stages.prompt: Choose the 90-day operating plan:

options.label: Pause open reqs; freeze non-quota S&M spend; reallocate 2 AEs to best segments; raise prices 8% on new logos; target CAC <$10k and payback <14 mo; weekly cash + unit-econ dashboard
options.rationale: Attacks CAC/payback levers, protects core capacity, and installs leading cash metrics.

options.label: Double paid ads and hire 4 more AEs to grow out of the burn
options.rationale: Accelerates cash burn while unit economics are broken — classic death spiral.

options.label: Cut R&D by 40% and keep S&M intact
options.rationale: May extend runway short-term but risks product stagnation and NRR; does not fix CAC quality.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate impact on unit economics, runway, and growth quality.

stages.prompt: Draft the 5-bullet board narrative: situation, root cause, 90-day actions, cash path, ask.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User drafted {response}. Evaluate clarity, numbers, accountability, and whether the ask matches the plan.
stages.sample_answer: 1) 8 mo runway, CAC 14k, LTV/CAC 2.1x. 2) Root: CAC inflation + win-rate drop, not pure opex bloat. 3) 90-day: freeze non-quota S&M, segment focus, +8% price new logos, weekly unit-econ. 4) Cut $120k/mo burn → ~10 mo runway. 5) Ask: approve plan; revisit bridge only if payback >16 mo at day 90.

optimal.title: Unit Economics Recovered
optimal.description: CAC back under $10k, payback 13 months, burn $275k. Board green-lights efficient growth; optional clean bridge avoided.

acceptable.title: Cash Stabilized, Growth Flat
acceptable.description: Runway extended to 12 months but NRR stuck near 100%. Need product-led expansion next quarter.

failure.title: Bridge on Weak Terms
failure.description: Burn unaddressed; raised down-round bridge with heavy preference. Morale crash and 18-month path to another crisis.

title: Series B Fundraising Terms
description: You have a term sheet at $80M post with 1x non-participating pref. A second investor offers higher valuation with ratchets. Choose and negotiate.

context.company: SaaS, $9M ARR, 110% NRR, 25% YoY growth accelerating to 40%, $6M cash, 14 mo runway
context.situation: Raising $20M Series B. Lead A: $80M post, 1x non-participating, pro-rata, standard protective provisions, 4-year employee option pool top-up to 12%. Lead B: $100M post, 1x participating preferred, full-ratchet anti-dilution, two board seats, 15% pool.
context.time_pressure: Exclusivity with Lead A expires in 5 days. Lead B wants answer in 72 hours.
data_provided: Current cap: founder 42%, seed 18%, Series A 28%, pool 8%, other 4%
Comps: growth-stage SaaS at 8-12x ARR; your growth supports ~9-10x if clean terms
Use of proceeds: 50% S&M, 30% product, 20% GTM infrastructure
Legal note: participating pref + full ratchet heavily favor investor on mediocre exits
Relationship: Lead A is existing Series A major; Lead B is new brand-name fund

stages.prompt: What frameworks matter most when comparing these term sheets?

options.label: Cap table waterfall modeling + liquidation preference economics + control rights analysis (not headline valuation alone)
options.rationale: Post-money is incomplete without prefs, participation, anti-dilution, and board control.

options.label: Always take the higher valuation — signals strength to the market
options.rationale: Toxic terms can destroy founder/common outcomes even at higher paper valuation.

options.label: Only compare dilution percentage to founders
options.rationale: Dilution matters but ignores liquidation waterfalls and governance risk.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain term sheet economics beyond headline price.

stages.prompt: At a $60M exit (below post), roughly compare common proceeds under Lead A (1x non-participating) vs Lead B (1x participating). Assume $20M new money is senior preferred. Explain qualitatively with rough math.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User analyzed {response}. Key point: at a down/ mediocre exit, participating pref lets Lead B take 1x then share remaining pro-rata, crushing common vs non-participating which converts or takes 1x. Full ratchet worsens future downs. Evaluate.
stages.sample_answer: At $60M exit with $20M senior pref: non-participating investor chooses max(1x=$20M, as-converted share). Participating takes $20M preference then also shares residual — common receives less. Full ratchet further dilutes common if future down rounds.

stages.prompt: What do you do?

options.label: Accept Lead A economics; use Lead B as leverage to improve A only on minor points (pool, pro-rata). Decline participating + full ratchet.
options.rationale: Clean terms + relationship continuity; avoids structural value transfer and control loss.

options.label: Take Lead B at $100M post to maximize paper valuation
options.rationale: Headline win, long-term misalignment and adverse waterfalls.

options.label: Run a process for 6 more weeks to create a bidding war
options.rationale: May work with long runway; here 14 mo and exclusivity clocks make delay risky without clear superior options.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate governance, economics, and timing tradeoffs.

stages.prompt: Write the founder email to the board recommending a path (5-8 sentences).
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User drafted {response}. Evaluate whether recommendation is clear, numbers-backed, and addresses control + liquidation risk.
stages.sample_answer: Recommend Lead A: clean 1x non-participating at fair 9x ARR, existing relationship, standard control. Decline Lead B despite higher post due to participating pref, full ratchet, and dual board seats. Use B only as leverage on pool sizing. Request board approval to sign A exclusivity extension if needed for counsel redlines.

optimal.title: Clean Round Closed
optimal.description: Closed Lead A with minor pool tweak. Cap table remains founder-friendly. Hired GTM leads; hit plan within 2 quarters.

acceptable.title: Slightly Compromised Terms
acceptable.description: Took hybrid: higher valuation but stripped participation. Slightly more complexity; still workable.

failure.title: Toxic Paper
failure.description: Accepted participating + full ratchet. Later flat round triggered ratchet; founder ownership crushed; painful secondary politics.

title: Enterprise Contract Negotiation
description: A Fortune 500 prospect wants 40% discount, unlimited liability, and annual termination for convenience. Worth 18% of next-year ARR target.

context.company: B2B SaaS, $15M ARR, average deal $40k, this opportunity $450k ACV (3-year proposed)
context.situation: Procurement opened at 40% off list, unlimited liability, security addenda, most-favored-nation, and termination for convenience on 30 days. Champion is strong; economic buyer is CFO-driven. Your list is $750k/3yr; you need this logo for enterprise reference.
context.time_pressure: Their fiscal year ends in 3 weeks. If missed, delay 6+ months.
data_provided: Your floor historically: 20% off multi-year with liability capped at 12 mo fees
BATNA: two mid-market deals totaling $180k ACV in pipeline this quarter
Competitor in deal: weaker product, known to discount 50%+
Legal red lines: unlimited liability and MFN are company policy blocks without CRO+GC
Expansion potential: 3 more divisions (~$1.2M ACV) if land successful

stages.prompt: How do you frame this negotiation before the next call?

options.label: Map BATNA/ZOPA, separate price from risk terms, list trades (term length, prepay, liability cap, reference rights)
options.rationale: Principled, multi-variable negotiation beats single-issue discounting.

options.label: Accept 40% off to win the logo; fix legal later
options.rationale: Sets deadly precedent; unlimited liability is existential, not cosmetic.

options.label: Walk immediately — any pushback means bad customer
options.rationale: Ignores expansion value and normal enterprise procurement theater.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate negotiation preparation quality.

stages.prompt: Estimate a defensible ZOPA on price for a 3-year deal. State your reservation price and a package anchor.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User estimated {response}. Strong answers cite ~20% floor ($600k/3yr), package with multi-year + liability cap + case study, and avoid matching 40% without trades. Evaluate.
stages.sample_answer: Reservation ~$600k/3yr (20% off) with liability capped at 12 months fees. Anchor package: $675k/3yr, 2-year minimum, Q1 prepay discount 5%, mutual liability cap, reference rights after go-live. 40% only if impossible without killing deal — then require longer term + expansion commitment.

stages.prompt: Procurement rejects and re-anchors at 35% off + unlimited liability. Your move:

options.label: Hold liability red line; offer 22% off for 3-year + annual prepay + phased liability (higher for data breach only with insurance); trade MFN for logo rights
options.rationale: Protects existential risk, uses trades, stays inside ZOPA.

options.label: Match 35% and accept unlimited liability to close before fiscal year-end
options.rationale: Catastrophic risk and margin destruction for one logo.

options.label: Escalate with a hard walk-away email to the CFO
options.rationale: May work as BATNA signal but burns champion path; better as calibrated consequence after a final package.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate risk management and deal craft.

stages.prompt: Write the short note to your champion summarizing the mutual-gain package (not a legal redline dump).
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User drafted {response}. Evaluate clarity, multi-issue framing, and champion enablement.
stages.sample_answer: We can land this before FYE with a 3-year agreement near 20-22% off list, annual prepay for extra savings, and security terms that meet your audit needs. We cannot accept unlimited liability (insurer + board policy) but will offer industry-standard breach caps backed by insurance. If you can move procurement off unlimited liability and MFN, we will prioritize implementation resources for a 45-day go-live.

optimal.title: Logo Won Cleanly
optimal.description: Closed at 21% off, 3-year, capped liability. Reference secured. Two divisions entered pipeline within 6 months.

acceptable.title: Deal Closed with Scars
acceptable.description: 25% discount and heavy security process; liability capped. Margin thin but precedent contained with deal desk approval.

failure.title: Bad Precedent
failure.description: Accepted deep discount + toxic liability. Three other enterprises demanded MFN. One incident claim threatened the company.

title: Strategic Partnership Negotiation
description: A platform giant offers distribution that could 3x pipeline — in exchange for exclusivity and rev-share that may cap your upside.

context.company: Vertical SaaS, $7M ARR, strong niche, limited enterprise distribution
context.situation: MegaPlatform wants 3-year partnership: feature them as preferred solution in-app, co-sell motion, 25% rev-share on influenced ARR, category exclusivity (no rival platforms), and 180-day termination only for cause. Your alternative is building your own channel (18-month payback).
context.time_pressure: Partnership team changes in 6 weeks; next sponsor unknown.
data_provided: Modeled influenced ARR: $2M Y1, $5M Y2, $9M Y3 if exclusive placement holds
Rev-share cost at 25%: large COGS-like hit; GM impact ~8-12pts on influenced revenue
Exclusivity blocks two smaller partners that could deliver $1.5M combined by Y2
Legal: data processing + brand guidelines heavy but manageable
BATNA: hire 3 partner managers + integrations budget $1.2M over 18 months

stages.prompt: What is the core negotiation problem?

options.label: Integrative deal design: expand pie (placement SLAs, co-marketing, non-exclusive tiers) rather than only arguing rev-share %
options.rationale: Interests differ: they want category control and monetization; you want distribution without strategic lock-in.

options.label: Pure distributive fight: minimize rev-share only
options.rationale: Important but incomplete — exclusivity and termination may matter more long-term.

options.label: Accept quickly before the sponsor leaves
options.rationale: Time pressure is real but rushing lock-in is how platforms capture all surplus.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate integrative vs distributive framing.

stages.prompt: Compare 3-year NPV-style qualitative value: exclusive 25% rev-share path vs non-exclusive multi-partner path. Call key risks.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User analyzed {response}. Strong answers weigh influenced ARR minus rev-share, exclusivity opportunity cost, platform dependency risk, and BATNA channel build cost. Evaluate.
stages.sample_answer: Exclusive path: higher top-line influenced ARR but 25% tax + concentration risk if placement deprioritized. Multi-partner: slower ramp, lower fees, diversified dependency, preserves options. Key risk: exclusivity without placement SLAs or opt-out is asymmetric.

stages.prompt: Choose your negotiation package to table:

options.label: 15% rev-share, 18-month limited exclusivity with performance gates (pipeline + sourced ARR), 90-day exit if gates miss, co-marketing fund, no MFN on future partners
options.rationale: Creates mutual gain, time-boxes exclusivity, ties value to performance.

options.label: Accept 25% and full 3-year exclusivity as written
options.rationale: Transfers too much value and strategic optionality.

options.label: Reject partnership entirely and only build direct channel
options.rationale: Valid BATNA but leaves distribution value on the table if terms can be fixed.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate strategic optionality and partnership economics.

stages.prompt: Draft the 1-page internal decision memo recommendation for the exec team.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User drafted {response}. Evaluate structure: context, options, recommendation, risks, metrics.
stages.sample_answer: Recommend counter with performance-gated exclusivity and lower rev-share. Proceed only if gates + exit rights accepted. Metrics: sourced pipeline, win rate, GM after rev-share, dependency %. Fallback: walk to multi-partner BATNA.

optimal.title: Performance-Gated Partnership
optimal.description: Closed 15% rev-share with 18-month exclusivity gates. Hit Y1 influenced ARR; retained right to add partners later.

acceptable.title: Narrower Distribution Win
acceptable.description: Non-exclusive listing at 12% rev-share. Slower growth but strategic freedom preserved.

failure.title: Platform Lock-In
failure.description: 3-year exclusivity at 25%. Placement deprioritized after reorg; growth stalled and rivals took other channels.

title: Ops Bottleneck: Theory of Constraints
description: Order-to-cash cycle doubled. Customers complain. Every department asks for more headcount. Find and elevate the constraint.

context.company: Hardware-enabled SaaS, $25M ARR, ships kits + cloud subscription, 200 employees
context.situation: Median order-to-cash time rose from 14 to 28 days. NPS ops score down 18pts. Inventory up, rush freight up 3x. Sales blames warehouse; warehouse blames incomplete orders; finance blames credit checks; engineering blames custom configs.
context.time_pressure: Peak season in 6 weeks. Board ops review in 2 weeks.
data_provided: Process stages avg days: Quote 2, Config 9 (was 3), Credit 2, Pick/Pack 4, Ship 2, Invoice 3, Collect 6
WIP: 120 orders stuck in Config queue; Config team = 4 specialists, utilization 96%
Defects: 22% of orders return to Config for rework after sales handoff
Pareto: 80% delay hours from Config + rework loops; freight overage $180k/quarter
Proposed asks: +3 warehouse, +2 AR, +1 salesperson, overtime budget

stages.prompt: Using Theory of Constraints, where do you focus first?

options.label: Identify the system constraint: Config queue (highest WIP, 96% util, drives rework). Do not hire non-constraints yet.
options.rationale: TOC: throughput is gated by the bottleneck; improving non-constraints increases WIP and cost.

options.label: Approve all headcount requests to reduce every queue
options.rationale: Local optimization; misses constraint and burns cash.

options.label: Cut SKUs by 50% immediately without process data
options.rationale: May help later but skips constraint analysis; sales impact unmodeled.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain TOC five focusing steps vs local efficiency.

stages.prompt: Apply DMAIC briefly: what metric defines success in 6 weeks, and what is the vital few (Pareto) to attack in Config?
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User answered {response}. Strong: primary metric order-to-cash median or Config cycle time; vital few = rework from incomplete sales handoffs + specialist capacity. Evaluate.
stages.sample_answer: Success metric: median order-to-cash ≤18 days and Config queue <40 orders before peak. Vital few: (1) sales handoff completeness checklist to cut 22% rework (2) protect Config capacity from non-urgent custom work (3) standard configs for top 20% SKUs covering 80% volume.

stages.prompt: Choose the 30-day action plan:

options.label: Exploit constraint: freeze non-critical custom configs; introduce sales config checklist; daily WIP board; cross-train 2 adjacent staff into Config; only then consider +1 Config specialist
options.rationale: TOC: exploit then subordinate then elevate — checklist and WIP control before throwing bodies.

options.label: Add 3 warehouse staff and expand overtime
options.rationale: Non-constraint; inventory and freight symptoms persist.

options.label: Replace ERP in 90 days
options.rationale: Too slow for peak season; high risk distraction.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate TOC discipline and time-to-impact.

stages.prompt: Write the all-hands ops note explaining why we are not hiring warehouse yet.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User drafted {response}. Evaluate clarity of constraint logic, empathy, and concrete asks of sales/config.
stages.sample_answer: Our bottleneck is Config, not the warehouse. Hiring warehouse first would pile more WIP behind Config. For 30 days we protect Config capacity, require complete handoffs, and standardize top SKUs. Warehouse overtime is temporary only. We will reassess staffing after Config queue halves.

optimal.title: Constraint Elevated
optimal.description: Config cycle to 4 days, order-to-cash 16 days, freight overages down 40%. Peak season cleared without panic hiring.

acceptable.title: Partial Flow Recovery
acceptable.description: Order-to-cash 21 days. Still some rework; need productized configs next quarter.

failure.title: Local Optimization Trap
failure.description: Hired warehouse/AR; Config still stuck. Inventory ballooned; peak season missed SLAs; NPS fell further.

title: Turnaround: Cash & Operations
description: New CEO of a distressed division: negative cash, slipping quality, and a parent company mandate to stabilize in 13 weeks or divest.

context.company: Industrial software + services division, $40M revenue, -$6M FCF trailing twelve, 320 employees
context.situation: Parent appointed you CEO to stop the bleed. Receivables at 78 DSO, delivery projects 30% over budget, top customer (12% revenue) threatening churn over quality, and a union negotiation in 60 days. Parent: 13-week cash plan or strategic alternatives.
context.time_pressure: 13-week cash plan due in 10 days; weekly parent reviews thereafter.
data_provided: Cash: $2.1M division cash, weekly burn ~$400k including project overruns
AR: $9M outstanding; $3.2M >90 days; disputes tied to delivery acceptance
Backlog: $18M but margin dilute — average project GM 22% vs bid 35%
Quality: escaped defects up 2x; rework labor $1.1M/quarter
People: critical architects flight risk; open leadership roles in CS and Delivery

stages.prompt: What is the correct turnaround sequence?

options.label: Stabilize cash (13-week forecast, AR blitz, spend freeze) → fix operations/quality on the constraint → then growth. Transparent parent cadence.
options.rationale: Classic turnaround playbook: cash first, then ops, then strategy.

options.label: Launch a bold new product vision to inspire the team
options.rationale: Vision without cash and delivery control accelerates failure.

options.label: Immediate 25% layoff day one without cash diagnostics
options.rationale: May be needed later but blind cuts can remove revenue-critical delivery capacity and worsen AR disputes.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate turnaround sequencing.

stages.prompt: Build a 13-week cash focus list: top 3 cash in levers and top 3 cash out levers with rough weekly impact.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User listed {response}. Strong answers include AR collections on >90 day, acceptance unblocking, vendor payment terms, hiring freeze, discretionary cut, project scope control. Evaluate realism.
stages.sample_answer: In: (1) AR tiger team on $3.2M >90d (2) acceptance milestones with top accounts (3) require deposits on new projects. Out: (1) hiring freeze + contractor cut (2) discretionary/marketing pause (3) stop non-profitable project scope creep. Target +$200-300k weekly swing vs status quo.

stages.prompt: Parent offers a $5M inject if you commit to a plan. Choose:

options.label: Take inject only with 13-week plan: AR war room, delivery stage-gates, quality containment on top customer, weekly FCF OKRs; no new logo hunting until GM recovery
options.rationale: Capital with operational discipline; avoids using inject to fund denial.

options.label: Take inject and invest entirely in a new sales surge
options.rationale: Sells more unprofitable work into a broken delivery system.

options.label: Refuse inject and threaten resignation to get a better deal
options.rationale: Theatrics over plan; parent will choose divestment.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate capital discipline in turnarounds.

stages.prompt: Draft the week-1 message to employees: honesty + priorities + what will not change yet.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User drafted {response}. Evaluate candor, cash/ops focus, and psychological safety without false certainty.
stages.sample_answer: We are in a cash and delivery crisis, not a mystery. Week 1-4 priorities: collect cash, stop defective releases to our top accounts, and freeze non-essential spend. We will not announce a vision reset or mass reorganization this week. Leaders will publish a 13-week scoreboard. Need your help unblocking acceptances and quality — not heroics on new features.

optimal.title: Stabilized Division
optimal.description: 13-week plan hit: DSO to 55, FCF breakeven by week 12, top customer retained. Parent continues investment.

acceptable.title: Controlled Distressed Sale Prep
acceptable.description: Cash stabilized enough to run an orderly strategic process with better terms than a fire sale.

failure.title: Value Destruction
failure.description: Inject spent on growth theater. AR worsened, quality incident with top customer, parent divests at distressed multiple.

title: Platform vs Solutions Org Design
description: Your product org is stuck between a platform team that owns shared services and solutions teams that ship customer value. Lead time is up 40%.

context.company: B2B product company, 180 engineers, 3 product lines, shared data platform
context.situation: Solutions squads bypass the platform for speed. Platform team measures API adoption; business measures revenue. A critical customer demo is in 6 weeks.
context.time_pressure: Board wants a 90-day plan to cut cycle time without growing headcount.
data_provided: Median feature lead time: 42 days (was 30)
Platform SLA: 99.5% but change lead time 14 days
Solutions teams reimplemented auth 3 times this year
NPS for internal platform: 18

stages.prompt: What is the primary structural problem?

options.label: Misaligned team boundaries and incentives between platform and solutions
options.rationale: Team topologies + Conway — structure drives communication and ownership

options.label: Engineers are not working hard enough
options.rationale: Ignores systemic design; pure effort narrative

options.label: Need a bigger PMO to approve all work
options.rationale: Adds coordination tax without fixing ownership

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate structural diagnosis quality.

stages.prompt: Propose a 90-day org operating model change (2-4 bullets). Name the interaction mode between platform and solutions.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User wrote {response}. Evaluate against Team Topologies interaction modes (X-as-a-Service, Collaboration, Facilitating) and incentive alignment.
stages.sample_answer: Move platform to X-as-a-Service for auth/data; temporary Collaboration for the demo path; solutions own customer outcomes with platform SLOs; shared OKR on lead time.

stages.prompt: Choose the first executive action:

options.label: Freeze new platform features for 6 weeks; staff a tiger team with platform+solutions for the demo path; publish platform SLOs and self-serve docs.
options.rationale: Unblocks value + clarifies platform product contract

options.label: Mandate all code go through platform review board
options.rationale: Central bottleneck worsens lead time

options.label: Split into three fully independent product companies immediately
options.rationale: May be long-term right; too disruptive for 90-day board plan

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate execution risk and learning speed.

optimal.title: Success
optimal.description: You balanced platform leverage with customer delivery.

title: Executive Team Conflict on Priorities
description: CRO and CPO openly disagree in the exec meeting. The roadmap is overloaded. You are CEO and must restore decision rights without losing either leader.

context.situation: Sales committed enterprise custom features; product wants platform purity. NPS slipping. Two VPs have started emailing board members.
context.time_pressure: All-hands in 10 days; QBR next week.
data_provided: Pipeline: 35% of deals blocked on custom work
Engineering capacity: 60% roadmap, 25% support, 15% tech debt
Attrition of senior PMs: 3 in 6 months
Board sentiment: concerned about execution, not strategy

stages.prompt: What should you clarify first?

options.label: Decision rights (RAPA/RACI) for roadmap vs deal exceptions
options.rationale: Conflict is often unclear authority, not personality

options.label: Who is more senior politically
options.rationale: Escalates factionalism

options.label: Fire one of them before the all-hands
options.rationale: Premature; loses institutional knowledge

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate leadership diagnosis.

stages.prompt: Select the process to run this week:

options.label: Facilitated crucial conversation with CRO+CPO; joint exception policy (threshold, capacity tax, sunset); single source-of-truth OKRs; board pre-brief with one narrative.
options.rationale: Rebuilds trust + decision system

options.label: Publicly back Sales in all-hands
options.rationale: Destroys product trust

options.label: Ignore and hope QBR numbers save the narrative
options.rationale: Conflict will leak to board

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate conflict resolution design.

stages.prompt: Write the exception policy in 3 rules the org can remember.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User wrote {response}. Good policies are clear, capacity-aware, and time-boxed.
stages.sample_answer: 1) Deals > custom require CRO+CPO dual approve. 2) Custom work consumes solutions capacity with 1.5x tax. 3) All exceptions expire in 2 quarters or become product.

optimal.title: Success
optimal.description: You restored decision rights and a shared narrative.

acceptable.title: Partial
acceptable.description: Tension reduced but policy may be vague.

title: Geopolitical Supply Shock
description: A key manufacturing region faces export restrictions. 40% of COGS is exposed. Customers ask for assurance letters.

context.situation: Export license delays hit your primary CM. Secondary CM has 30% higher unit cost and 16-week ramp. Public markets are asking about guidance.
context.time_pressure: Earnings call in 3 weeks; customer SLAs at risk in 45 days.
data_provided: Inventory: 8 weeks finished goods, 4 weeks WIP
Gross margin: 52% (was 58% last year)
Top 10 customers: 55% of revenue
Secondary CM quote: +30% unit cost, NRE .1M, 16 weeks

stages.prompt: Which analytical frame first?

options.label: Scenario planning + value chain exposure (base/adverse/severe)
options.rationale: Uncertainty needs scenarios, not a single forecast

options.label: Only cut price to keep share
options.rationale: Ignores supply constraint

options.label: Wait for regulators to clarify before any action
options.rationale: Loses option value and customer trust

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate under deep uncertainty.

stages.prompt: Estimate quarterly gross margin if 40% of volume moves to the secondary CM at +30% unit COGS. State assumptions.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User estimated {response}. Reasonable: mix-weighted COGS up ~12% of total COGS on that volume; margin compression depends on price pass-through.
stages.sample_answer: If 40% volume at 1.3x COGS and 60% unchanged, blended COGS up ~12%. At 52% GM, roughly ~6pt GM hit before pricing if fully absorbed.

stages.prompt: Choose the portfolio response:

options.label: Dual-source ramp with real-options staged NRE; allocate scarce units to strategic customers; transparent guidance band; temporary price/SLA matrix.
options.rationale: Builds optionality + trust

options.label: Promise all customers no change in price or delivery
options.rationale: Sets up miss

options.label: Exit the product line this quarter
options.rationale: May be later option; destroys value if premature

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate resilience and communications.

optimal.title: Success
optimal.description: You preserved options and customer trust under uncertainty.
